clues.NEAR: Close enough for the folded sections to stay side by side

town-service-desks-3.solvingTip: Start with what the clerk hands you as proof of payment. For the stamp strip, look for one clue that asks for an action and one that names the bundle.

clues.COIL: Wind a loose strip of stamps into a spiral
clues.ROLL: Bundle of postage stamps sold as one long wound strip

notes.ROLL: A roll of postage stamps is a whole strip wound tightly. The clerk can sell it as one bundle.

kitchen-preparation.solvingTip: Start with the vegetable and the tool beside it. For the cutting clues, think about the shape of the pieces and how the blade moves.

clues.DICE: Cut the onion into small, even cubes
clues.CHOP: Cut the onion into rough pieces using several quick strokes
clues.PEEL: Remove the dry outer skin from an onion

restful-household-routines-4.solvingTip: Think of getting ready for a walk. Start with the soft layer that goes on first, then find the footwear that meets the sidewalk.

clues.CUSHION: Soft padding that makes a walking shoe feel gentler underfoot
clues.SOCK: Soft knit garment worn inside a shoe
clues.SHOE: Footwear with a sturdy sole for walking outside

by-the-sea-3.solvingTip: Start with the short clue for a raised line on a fan-shaped shell. For the sea snail clues, look for a pointed spiral and for the shell sometimes used as a horn.

clues.WHELK: Sea snail with a spiral shell that often ends in a long point
clues.CONCH: Large sea snail whose shell is sometimes blown like a horn

saved-messages-5.solvingTip: Start with the short word for what a passenger pays. Then find the little bag that keeps a token apart from the loose coins.

clues.POUCH: Small soft bag, such as a drawstring bag holding one token
clues.PURSE: Small bag carried to hold loose change

notes.PURSE: A coin purse keeps loose change together. A token set apart from the coins is easier to find before boarding.

halloween-evening-2.solvingTip: Try the clue for what changes a wearer's face. For the costume bands, look for one across the shoulder and one fastened at the waist.

clues.SASH: Decorative cloth band that can cross from shoulder to hip
clues.BELT: Strap often buckled around the waist

notes.SASH: A costume sash can hang across the chest from one shoulder to the opposite hip.

summer-afternoons-5.solvingTip: Start with the cord used to tie up a boat. For the two boat clues, look at how many blades each boat's usual paddle has.

clues.CANOE: Open boat usually moved with a paddle with one blade

notes.CANOE: Canoe paddles usually have one blade. A paddler can switch sides to keep the boat moving straight.

community-notices-3.solvingTip: Start with where the visitor sets down the chair near the door. Then look for the word for using a neighbor's chair with permission for a short time.

clues.BORROW: Take a chair to use for a short time with the owner's permission

looking-at-the-shore.solvingTip: Start with the part the crab uses to grip. Then look for the small patch of seawater that can stay behind as the sea pulls away.

clues.WATER: Salty liquid that wets the sand at the shore
clues.POOL: Small body of water left in a dip in the beach

notes.WATER: As the tide goes out, some seawater can stay behind in low areas of the beach.

games-remembered-4.solvingTip: Picture the toy with one part in your hand and another at the end of a stretchy cord. Try the shorter word for the round part first.

clues.PADDLE: Flat wooden piece used to hit the ball on the elastic cord
clues.RETURN: Come back toward the hand after the cord stretches

fall-harvest-work-2.solvingTip: Start with what you wear on your hands to gather the nuts. Then distinguish the thick cover from the hard layer underneath it.

clues.ROUGH: Uneven to the touch, like a wrinkled nut shell
clues.STAIN: Dark mark a walnut husk can leave on your hands

older-cars-and-bicycles-2.solvingTip: Start with the short American word for what you buy at the pump. Then think about what the pointer shows when very little remains in the tank.

clues.SCALE: Row of marks between empty and full on a fuel gauge
clues.DRIVE: Go somewhere by operating a car
clues.LOW: Close to empty, as a fuel tank may be

a-rest-stop-on-the-road.solvingTip: Start with what tells the driver the stop is ahead. Then look for the side-by-side strips of road and the turnoff that leads to the stop.

clues.DRIVE: Operate a car on the way to the rest stop
clues.GOAL: Something a driver is trying to do, such as reaching a rest stop
clues.LANE: Marked strip of road wide enough for one line of cars

simple-summer-day-trips.solvingTip: Try the three-letter clue for the drawing of roads. Then look for how you make it smaller and what keeps it from blowing away.

clues.DRIVE: Operate the car on the way to the picnic

small-town-outings-2.solvingTip: Start with what you use to dry off. Then picture where you put your things and where you rinse before or after the swim.

clues.SHOWER: Spray of water swimmers can rinse under

kitchen-jars-and-tins-5.solvingTip: Start with the color that beet rounds leave on a dish. Then look for what runs out of the jar and what it can do to the dish.

clues.STAIN: Leave a mark on the plate, as beet liquid can
clues.JUICE: Red liquid that can drain from sliced beets
clues.RED: Color left by the beet liquid

notes.RED: Beet pigments can give the liquid a deep red color.
notes.JUICE: Liquid from sliced beets can spread across a plate and leave a colored mark.

fittings-in-shared-places-3.solvingTip: Start with the long seat the sign is beside. Then read the clues about the new layer and what can happen if someone touches it too soon.

clues.STAIN: Colored mark wet paint can leave on clothing
clues.STICK: Adhere to a surface, as paper can to damp paint
clues.FRESH: Recently put on, as the paint on the seat
clues.COAT: One layer of paint on the wood

listening-with-old-equipment.solvingTip: Start with the piece your fingers turn. Then picture the small moving marker and the printed marks it passes as the broadcast comes through.

clues.SCALE: Row of printed marks a radio pointer moves along
clues.DIAL: Numbered face you look at when choosing a radio station
clues.BAND: Range of radio stations, such as the ones on AM
clues.KNOB: Rounded control you turn by hand to choose a station

autumn-outings.solvingTip: Start with what the wagon rolls on. Then look for the machine at the front and the narrow road it follows across the farm.

clues.LANE: Narrow road the tractor follows across the farm

games-at-a-club-3.solvingTip: Picture sending the ball toward the pins and getting it back. Start with the round object, then look for the floor it goes down and the path that brings it back.

clues.BALL: Heavy round object a bowler sends toward the pins
clues.TRACK: Path that guides the ball back to the bowlers
clues.LANE: Long strip of smooth floor the ball rolls down toward the pins
clues.ROLL: Send the ball moving along the floor so it turns over

notes.BALL: A bowling ball rolls down the lane toward the pins. A separate track guides it back.

errands-on-main-street-3.solvingTip: Start with the short clue for what you bring back. Then look for the opening where it can go and the mark that tells you when it was due.

clues.COVER: Protective front or back of a book
clues.STAMP: Mark a date on a library slip with ink
clues.SLOT: Narrow opening for books at a library return bin

notes.STAMP: A library date stamp can leave a printed mark on a slip to show when a book was due.

looking-at-the-shore-2.solvingTip: Start with the clue for one part of the star-shaped animal. Then think about where seawater stays when the tide has gone out.

clues.WATER: Liquid left among the rocks by the outgoing tide
clues.SHORE: Land along the edge of the sea
clues.POOL: Small body of water left between rocks after the tide falls
clues.LOW: Toward the bottom of the tide's usual range

notes.WATER: Water can remain in a dip between the rocks after the tide falls, forming a tide pool.

guitar-to-gathering-4.solvingTip: Start with what the player uses to hear the notes. Then look for the small part they turn and the word for how high or deep a note sounds.

clues.STRING: Thin strand stretched along a guitar that sounds when plucked
clues.PITCH: How high or deep a musical note sounds
clues.TUNE: Adjust the strings until the notes sound right
clues.TURN: Twist a peg to adjust how its string sounds
clues.PEG: Part you turn to tighten or loosen a guitar string
clues.LOW: Toward the deeper end of a musical range

notes.PITCH: Two notes have the same pitch when they sound equally high or deep.
notes.PEG: Turning a tuning peg changes the tension of its string.
notes.TUNE: To tune a guitar, adjust the strings until each plays the note you expect.

water-edges-after-weather-3.solvingTip: Start with the land beside the flowing water. Then find the small dip nearby where water can stay after the stream goes down.

clues.POCKET: Small hollow beside the stream that can hold water

warm-day-by-the-water-3.solvingTip: Start with the short word for where a boat can tie up. Then picture how the edge of the water moves when more of the ramp shows.

clues.WATER: Liquid that has dropped enough to expose more of the boat ramp
clues.LEVEL: Height of the water beside the ramp
clues.LOW: Below the usual height, as water near a dock may be

garden-harvest-baskets-3.solvingTip: Picture opening an ear of corn. Start with the outer leaves you pull back, then look for the fine threads inside.

clues.YELLOW: Color of many ripe corn kernels
clues.KERNEL: One small grain in a row on an ear of corn
clues.EAR: Part of the corn plant that holds kernels on a cob

notes.YELLOW: Yellow corn has kernels of that color arranged in rows along the cob.

garden-harvest-baskets-4.solvingTip: Start with the tool that loosens the mound. Once the potatoes are out, look for the word for one of the small buds on the surface.

clues.BROWN: Color of the skin on many baking potatoes
clues.SKIN: Thin outside covering of a potato
clues.PEEL: Remove a potato's skin before cooking

notes.PEEL: Here peel is the action of taking the outside layer off a potato.

garden-harvest-baskets-5.solvingTip: Start with what you do to clean the leaves. Then look for the clue that names the whole cluster on one plant.

clues.BASE: Lower part of the lettuce where the leaves join
clues.HEAD: Whole cluster of leaves on one lettuce plant

garden-small-spaces.solvingTip: Picture the plant on a kitchen windowsill. Start with the clue for what holds the soil, then look for the smell released by one leaf.

clues.SCENT: Pleasant smell released when you rub a basil leaf
clues.LIGHT: Brightness from a window that helps a potted herb grow
clues.TRAY: Flat piece that catches water beneath a plant pot

notes.SCENT: Basil leaves can release their familiar smell when you rub them between your fingers.

memories-of-schooldays-2.solvingTip: Start with the soft stick used to write the lesson. Then picture what the teacher rubs across the board to clear it.

clues.ERASER: Felt tool used to wipe chalk marks off a classroom board
clues.LETTER: Single mark of the alphabet, such as A or B
clues.DUST: Fine powder left when chalk marks are wiped away

notes.ERASER: A felt blackboard eraser picks up loose chalk powder when you rub it across the board.

memories-of-schooldays-3.solvingTip: Start with something you write with. Then look for what makes its point sharp and what closes over the supplies.

clues.PENCIL: Writing tool with a point you can sharpen
clues.LID: Top that closes over the box of pencils

memories-of-schooldays-4.solvingTip: Start with the sound that sends the class outside. Then picture where the children queue up and where they go to play.

clues.LINE: Row of children waiting by the classroom door
clues.YARD: Outdoor area at a school where children play
clues.RING: Make the sound that signals time for recess

errands-on-main-street.solvingTip: Start with what people form while waiting their turn. Then look for the clues for the worker, the work surface and the paper you get after paying.

clues.LINE: Row of people waiting to be helped at the counter

errands-on-main-street-4.solvingTip: Start with the person who takes the money. Then find the paper you fill in and the separate paper that confirms the deposit.

clues.RECEIPT: Paper confirming money was put into your bank account
clues.COUNT: Find the amount by adding the bills and coins
clues.NOTE: Piece of paper money, such as a dollar bill
clues.DESK: Worktable where a teller can handle bank forms

notes.NOTE: A banknote is one piece of paper money. Its value is printed on it.
notes.COIN: Coins are pieces of metal used as money. The teller can count them separately from bills.

errands-on-main-street-5.solvingTip: Start with the paper you show to collect your clothes. Then look for what the cleaned clothes hang from and what the worker checks on the paper.

clues.TICKET: Small paper you show to claim clothes you left for cleaning

notes.TICKET: The number on a claim ticket helps match cleaned clothes to the customer who left them.

breakfast-from-the-stove-3.solvingTip: Start with what you use to eat the warm cereal. Then try the short clue for its grain and either of the two sweet toppings.

clues.THICK: Dense enough to move slowly when stirred, like oatmeal
clues.OAT: Grain cooked to make a familiar hot breakfast cereal

breakfast-from-the-stove-4.solvingTip: Think of the bread before it goes into the pan and after it comes out. Start with what a cook dips it into or what they pour over it to serve.

clues.BUTTER: Dairy fat often melted in a pan before browning bread
clues.TOAST: French ___, bread dipped in egg and browned for breakfast
clues.SYRUP: Sweet liquid poured over warm French toast
clues.MILK: White liquid some cooks whisk with eggs for French toast

quiet-table-hobbies-2.solvingTip: Start with what sticks the tiny parts together. Then look for one short word for a part at the back and a longer one for what spins at the front.

clues.PROPELLER: Spinning part that helps an airplane move forward
clues.TAIL: Rear part of an airplane, often with an upright fin

quiet-table-hobbies-3.solvingTip: Start with a single alphabet character or the tool that circles it. Then look for the ways a hidden word can run across the page.

clues.LETTER: One alphabet character in a square of the puzzle
clues.PENCIL: Writing tool used to circle words and erase mistakes
clues.DIAGONAL: Slanted line, like one running down and to the right

notes.LETTER: Each square holds a single letter. Neighboring letters form a word when you follow the right line.

quiet-table-hobbies-4.solvingTip: Try the clue for the whole pack you lay out. Then look at the colors and shapes of the symbols on individual cards.

notes.DECK: A standard deck has 52 cards divided among four suits.

songs-with-everyday-words-2.solvingTip: Start with what the batter holds and what the pitcher throws. Then look for the short word for cheering, as the song asks fans to do.

clues.FIELD: Ground where baseball players run and catch the ball
clues.BALL: Small round object a pitcher throws toward the batter
clues.BAT: Club a baseball player swings to hit the ball

notes.FIELD: The ball field includes the infield around the bases and the outfield beyond it.

animals-on-the-farm-2.solvingTip: Start with the short name of the mother or the young animal. Then find the part of the boundary that swings open.

clues.HOOF: Hard covering on the end of a calf's foot
clues.COW: Farm animal that is the mother of a calf

notes.FIELD: A farm field is an open piece of land. Some fields grow crops and others give cattle space to graze.

bible-beginnings-3.solvingTip: Start with the name of the man who builds the vessel. Then look for what it is made from and the number of animals that make up a matching group.

clues.WATER: Liquid that covers normally dry land in a flood
clues.BOAT: Vessel that travels or floats on water
clues.PAIR: Group of two animals that go together in the story

notes.WATER: In the story, the flood covers the land, and Noah's vessel floats as the water rises.

taking-care-of-small-supplies-3.solvingTip: Start with the shallow holder that goes under the bottles. Then find what splits it into spaces and the word for how the bottles stand.

clues.GROUP: Small set of bottles kept together in one part of the tray
